topic: How would the 0.25 dB passband loss affect link budget margins in low-noise satellite receiver frontends?
consensus_response: The 0.25 dB passband loss in low-noise satellite receiver frontends would compromise link budget margins by reducing the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and signal-to-interference ratio (SIR). This degradation would be exacerbated by frequency-selective fading, amplifier saturation, and third-order intermodulation distortion. As a result, the system's ability to maintain a reliable link would be compromised, leading to increased bit error rates and reduced capacity. To mitigate this effect, advanced interference mitigation techniques, equalization, and adaptive filtering would be necessary to maintain the required quality of service.
